author: marywuestner
caption: my favorite month to scrapbook yet🤍 Six months feels different. Her little personality is becoming so vibrant. She’s sitting up on her own, interacting with everything around her, making us laugh, trying new foods, and gaining just enough independence that I can see this tiny person she’s becoming. There’s so much joy in this season. And maybe that’s why putting these pages together felt especially healing. I’ve shared before that scrapbooking became an unexpected outlet for my postpartum anxiety. It gives me somewhere to put all of the emotions that come with watching time move this quickly — instead of wishing I could slow it down, I get to sit with it, remember it, and turn it into something we can keep. Six months of her. Six months of becoming her mom. And somehow, this chapter has been the sweetest one yet. 🥹💕 One day she’ll flip through these pages and see the milestones. I hope she also sees just how much joy she brought into every one of them. #scrapbooking #postpartum #firsttimemom #baby

author: forgetmenot_journals
caption:
We asked our Mum for one small thing, but what she wrote transformed our lives. 

We just asked her to write down a few things about her life, family jokes we didn’t want to forget, little anecdotes of her childhood she loved to share, which we wanted in her own words - to hold onto.

She wrote us a whole book. We learned so much about her. Things she had never spoken about. Unearthing memories even she hadn’t thought about in 50 years. She passed it onto us, and 10 years later, it inspired us to help other parents and grandparents write to their children too.

I don’t think Forget Me Not would have ever become what it is now, if it wasn’t for this journal.

Now, my sister and I work together every day, creating journals for your family stories. 

- Megan x

#ForgetMeNotJournals #FamilyKeepsakes #FamilyJournal #FamilyHeirloom #MemoryKeeping

author: storykeeping
caption:
I never had the opportunity to film my mom's dad, Grandpa Benke, so I interviewed my eldest aunt Barbara Rose to see what I could learn. 

The Benke Ranch (now Kyle Seale Ranch) neighbored John Igo's family, the Wollers, and one of my grandpa's favorite stories to tell involved him and his brothers thumping the Woller's watermelons. 

Imagine walking through the woods with your brothers a few miles to swim in a creek. Stopping to find the sweetest watermelon in the bunch. And when your brother plugs too many of the neighbor's watermelons, the next time you pass through you get a shotgun pulled on you. What a time to be alive.

author: miribh
caption:
25 years can sound like a long time. For families who lost someone on September 11, time is measured differently.

There are children who grew up without a parent. Grandchildren who know someone only through photographs and stories. Families who have built entire lives around an absence that never completely disappears.

Watching my husband carry the loss of his father has taught me something important about trauma: moving forward and remembering are not opposites.

We can grieve what should have been while still creating what comes next.

Today I’m thinking of James J. Hobin, the family he left behind, and every family still carrying someone forward 25 years later.

May their memories be a blessing.

#September11 #NeverForget #traumaticinvalidation #miribarhalpern #JamesJHobin

author: morgansmithmcbride
caption:
I’ll never regret saving these. 🥹
But I also don’t want boxes and boxes of school papers taking over my house.
So every year, each kid gets ONE binder for that school year.
As the papers come home, I save the ones I actually want to keep. A few times throughout the year, I go through the pile, hole punch everything, and add it to their binder.
Artwork, handwriting, funny little assignments, stories they wrote... all those tiny snapshots of who they were that year. ❤️
The best part? All of their school binders will fit into ONE bin per kid.
One bin of school memories from their whole childhood.
Easy to keep. Easy to look back on. And someday, I know I’ll be so glad I saved them.
